mainProgression.progression: E5 - Chromatic Walks - C5 - B5 - A5 - B5
mainProgression.description: High-velocity 212 BPM thrash masterpiece built on relentless downpicked open low E palm muting, chromatic fills, and meter shifts

sectionProgressions.description: Relentless all-downstroke palm-muted pedal tones on the open E string punctuated by chromatic stabs
Descending natural minor power chord sequence driving toward the climactic shout chorus
James Hetfield's neo-classical twin-guitar harmony solo in half-time providing breathtaking melodic contrast

harmonicFunction: E5 (i5) - The crushing open-string pedal foundation driving the thrash engine
C5 (bVI5) - Submediant punch providing dark minor key weight
B5 (V5) - Dominant anchor resolving back down to the open E tonic
F5 (bII5) - Neapolitan / Phrygian half-step dissonance creating extreme metal tension

techniques.name: High-Velocity Downpicking Endurance
techniques.description: Executing rapid 8th-note palm-muted rhythms entirely with downward pick strokes at 212 BPM, creating the percussive attack fundamental to thrash metal

notes: Zero alternate picking on the verse pedal tones—strict downstrokes only
Requires a compact, economic pick stroke focused in the wrist, not elbow
Maintain consistent palm muting on the bridge saddles
sequence: Rest fleshy edge of pick palm on low E saddle
Strike with sharp downward wrist snap
Return pick quickly above the string without striking on upstroke
tips: Start at 140 BPM and build stamina by 5 BPM increments weekly
Keep thumb and index grip relaxed to prevent forearm cramp
Use a rigid 1.0mm-1.14mm pick with a sharp tip (e.g., Dunlop Tortex or Hetfield Black Fang)

techniques.name: Odd-Meter Rhythmic Turnarounds (5/8 Time)
techniques.description: Mastering the disorienting 5/8 time measure inserted into the 4/4 verse groove that catches listeners off guard

notes: Three measures of 4/4 followed by one measure of 5/8
The 5/8 bar truncates the expected beat, giving the riff relentless forward momentum
sequence: Play 3 full bars of 4/4 verse riff
Drop 3 eighth notes on the 4th measure (5 eighth notes total)
Land hard on beat 1 of the next cycle
tips: Lock tightly with the snare drum accents

techniques.name: Twin-Guitar Diatonic Harmonies
techniques.description: Dual guitars playing in harmonized 3rds and 6ths across the E natural minor scale during the slow interlude

notes: Guitar 1 plays the primary melody in E minor
Guitar 2 plays a diatonic 3rd above in harmony
Requires matched vibrato rate and identical note duration
sequence: Sync note releases and vibrato with the harmony partner
Let chords breathe over the half-time drum groove
tips: Record one track first and practice playing the harmony against your own playback
Tune with extreme precision—minor 3rds will sound sour if either guitar is slightly sharp

sections.name: Iconic Chromatic Intro Riff
sections.description: The opening statement featuring aggressive power chord stabs followed by the famous chromatic single-note descent on strings 5 and 6
notes: Chromatic run: fret 7 down to fret 1 on the 5th and 6th strings
Mute low E between stabs with pick-hand palm

sections.name: Main Verse Riff (with 5/8 Turnaround)
sections.description: The driving 212 BPM engine of the song: three bars of 4/4 chugging followed by the sharp 5/8 meter cutoff
notes: All downstrokes at 212 BPM—no alternate picking!
Count the 5/8 bar with five eighth notes before looping back
Keep palm mute tight on the bridge for maximum percussive thud

sections.name: Interlude Harmonized Solo
sections.description: James Hetfield's slow, soulful neoclassical guitar solo played over gentle arpeggios, featuring dual guitar harmony in diatonic 3rds
notes: Switch to neck pickup for smooth, liquid sustain
Slow half-time feel allows notes to bloom with wide vibrato
Follows the chord progression closely with target notes on beat 1

guitar.recommended: ESP MX-220 / Explorer or Gibson Flying V with active EMG 81/60 humbuckers
alternatives: Jackson King V or Kelly with high-output pickups
guitar.pickup: Bridge EMG 81 active humbucker for tight, razor-sharp downpicking clarity

amp.recommended: Mesa/Boogie Mark IIC+ (Simul-Class) slaved into Marshall 1960B 4x12 with Celestion V30s

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer (Drive: 0, Level: 10, Tone: 6) used as a clean mid-boost in front of the amp
effects.reverb: Bypass during rhythm; subtle plate on the melodic interlude solo
effects.other: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah (used extensively by Kirk Hammett on the fast solo)

beginner.title: Build Downpicking Stamina & Learn Intro Riff
steps: Practice the chromatic descending intro riff at a slow 120 BPM
Learn the power chords for the chorus and pre-chorus
Develop forearm stamina using a metronome and strict downpicking

intermediate.title: Master the 5/8 Verse Meter & Melodic Interlude Solo
steps: Count and execute the 5/8 turnaround accurately at 160 BPM
Learn James Hetfield's slow interlude solo note-for-note
Coordinate twin guitar harmonies with a backing track

advanced.title: Full 212 BPM Performance & Kirk Hammett Solo
steps: Perform the full 8:35 track with all-downstroke rhythm at full 212 BPM
Learn Kirk's high-speed pentatonic shred and two-handed tapping phrases
Maintain razor-sharp palm muting and band synchronicity throughout

commonMistakes: Switching to alternate picking on the verse chugs—destroys the authentic percussive thud
Losing the beat on the 5/8 time bar—count aloud until your internal clock locks in
Tensing the shoulder and forearm—foster a loose, fluid wrist snap to prevent injury
practiceRoutine: 10 min: Slow metronome downpicking warm-up starting at 140 BPM, stepping up by 10 BPM
15 min: Verse riff isolation focusing on the 5/8 bar transition
15 min: Interlude melodic solo focusing on intonation and vibrato control
10 min: Full track run-through with metronome or backing track
focusAreas: Right-hand downpicking economy and wrist relaxation
High-gain palm mute tightness without deadening pitch
metronomeWork: Start verse riff at 140 BPM, increase by 5 BPM every 3 days until reaching 212 BPM
Set metronome to click only on beats 2 and 4 to test your internal tempo stability
